02 / Why now

Rules want a record.
Buyers want proof.

Each rule below needs a record most factories do not keep. Only 12% have the software for it, and agents now make keeping it cheap.

  1. APR 2023

    Audit trail

    Books in software, with an edit log that cannot be switched off.

  2. AUG 2023

    E-invoicing at ₹5 crore

    Every B2B invoice is registered on the government portal.

  3. APR 2024

    45-day payment rule

    Pay a small supplier late and lose the tax deduction.

  4. APR 2025

    30-day invoice window

    Above ₹10 crore, older invoices can no longer be reported.

  5. JUN 2025

    Peenya gets special status

    Our first cluster, about 13,000 industries, becomes a Special Investment Region.

  6. FY 2025–26

    Order platforms scale

    Zetwerk reports ₹15,913 crore across 6,979 suppliers. Buyers choose shops on proof.

  7. MAY 2026

    Business AI on WhatsAppREPORTED

    Agents can answer on the channel every supplier already uses.

  8. AUG 2026

    MSMED amendmentREPORTED

    Pushes more small-supplier invoices through TReDS. Text to be verified.

03 / How it works

Agents do the work.
People decide.

One order passes nine stations. The agent drafts, chases and posts at each one. Anything that commits money or stock waits for a person.

  • The agent drafts and chases

    It reads the customer’s PO from email, writes the supplier request from the BOM and quality plan, and chases replies.

  • A person decides

    Confirming, awarding, approving, releasing and paying stay with people. Above a limit, the owner signs on the phone.

  • The work writes the record

    A receipt, an inspection, a shipment and an on-time payment each update a record nobody can type into.

04 / Inside XELOR

Six roles.
One trusted record.

Purchase works on a laptop. The owner and the supplier use their phones. Stores uses a tablet at the gate. Every screen reads the same order.

  • The XELOR Agent shows what it did, what it is chasing and what needs you.
  • The supplier quotes from a message link or a voice note, with no login and no app.
  • Above a buyer’s limit, the purchase order goes to the owner’s phone.
  • Demonstration data, labelled on every screen. Agent steps are scripted.

06 / The record that compounds

Earned at the gate.
Never typed in.

A supplier’s record comes from what actually arrives. Nobody types a score.

01

Counted, not typed

On-time and reject rates come from goods receipts and incoming inspections.

Reads “unknown” until a delivery is counted.
02

Unproven means unproven

A supplier that has never delivered scores nothing for track record.

It never borrows anyone’s average.
03

The factory earns one too

Shipments, returns and on-time supplier payments write the factory’s own passport.

Shared with buyers as a read-only link.

Ranked with reasons.
A person decides.

Answers come back ranked, with the reasoning written out. The buyer awards, and above the buyer’s limit the owner approves.

RANKING WEIGHTS ARE A DESIGN PROPOSAL

  • Landed cost35%

07 / The network

Two records, written by the work.
Every request grows the network.

Suppliers join free. Factories book each other’s spare capacity with no cut. A record can’t be back-filled, so time in the network is the moat.

09 / Business model

Factories pay per plant.
Suppliers join free.

Every user in the plant is included, and so is the agent. The first payment is the pilot. Suppliers never pay.

Paid pilot₹3 L

Six weeks, one workflow, a signed baseline. Credited in full on conversion.

InstallationQuotedper plant

Data migration from Tally and spreadsheets, and commissioning. We do the setup ourselves.

One plant₹50k/ month

₹6 lakh a year. The whole plant, the agent, two standard connectors, every user included.

Suppliers₹0

A free record, quotes from a link and a capacity calendar. Extra plants join at a group rate.

5×

A pilot converts at full price only after it shows ₹30 lakh of measurable yearly value, five times the yearly fee, against a signed baseline.Launch prices under test. No customer has accepted them yet; they are fixed after five paid pilots in each segment.

Later, not live: a share of supplier early payment through TReDS partners, priced on the earned record. Capacity bookings between factories carry no fee.

11 / What must become defensible

Features are table stakes.
The record is the moat.

We do not win on features or sticker price. Here is what happens if others move.

If a funded AI agent moves down-market

It sits on someone else’s ERP

Didero, Mandel AI and Magentic read other systems. The record is counted where XELOR runs: at the gate.

If Tally, Zoho or IndiaMART + Busy go deeper

We start beside them

A network layer synced to Tally, Busy or Zoho, then the full ERP when the plant is ready. We do the setup ourselves.

If an order platform builds the record

They are outside the factory

Zetwerk and Wootz see their own orders. None of them sits where a delivery is counted.

Why the record wins

It cannot be back-filled

Dated deliveries and inspections build up with every receipt. It needs many plants in one cluster, which we have not built yet.

How we win the cluster

Density before spread
1

Ten plants that trade

Pilot factories in Peenya chosen because they buy from each other, so records start dense.

2

Start beside Tally

The network layer first, synced to the books they already keep. The full ERP when ready.

3

Every request invites

Suppliers claim free records. Their other buyers see them, and the cluster fills itself.

4

Then the next cluster

Hosur next door, then Coimbatore’s pump makers. Tiny (YC F24) chases the same factories; we win on GST, Indian languages and WhatsApp.
